$comment: Which probes can be run unattended, and which cannot.
This file is deliberately conservative and deliberately incomplete. A probe
is only listed as 'unattended' once somebody has actually run it that way and
watched it reach a verdict. Everything else is either listed with the reason
it needs a human, or left out entirely — and `npm run probe -- --list` shows
the unclassified ones as exactly that.
The alternative — assuming a probe is safe because its name sounds safe —
produces a harness that reports failures nobody trusts, which is worse than
having no harness. Add entries here as you verify them.

SLASH_SHIELD_WARMUP_PROBE.note: Renderer lifecycle and history side effects of the shield warm-up. Local only.

SLASH_YT_TIMING_PROBE.note: Loads real YouTube watch pages and asks whether the ad strip ran. Needs a network and a clean profile.

manual.SLASH_AUTOHIDE_PROBE: Needs a real pointer moved by something outside the process. `sendInputEvent` cannot test what the window manager decides, and a version built on it passed against the bug.
manual.SLASH_YT_ADS_PROBE: Cannot currently run its A/B at all: `autoplayPolicy: 'user-gesture-required'` means a scripted play() is refused and the player never lays out under automation.
manual.SLASH_SIGNIN_PROBE: Needs a real Google account and a live Supabase project.
manual.SLASH_GOOGLE_UA_PROBE: Loads Google's real sign-in form; meaningful only when watched.
manual.SLASH_INSTALL_PROBE: Touches the updater's install path. Run it deliberately, not as part of a sweep.
manual.SLASH_UPDATE_PROBE: Talks to the release feed and can download a package.
